appraisal_events.evidence: l'ambassadrice loue la Princesse en excès puis dénigre Oriane par comparaison ('Marie-Gilbert, c'est quelqu'un'); le narrateur note ensuite qu'une invitation refusée ou reçue détermine son jugement, et conclut qu'elle est une 'fausse étoile', une simple 'figurante' utile mais non une vraie grande dame.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator exposes the ambassadrice's lavish praise of the princesse and dismissal of the duchesse as socially reactive rather than independently grounded, and closes by classing her among decorative 'figurantes' rather than genuine society stars, locally lowering her standing as both judge and social figure.

appraisal_events.evidence: 'il ne passa pas inaperçu aux yeux du duc... [qui] avait été émerveillé de mon salut, qu'il était impossible d'y faire tenir plus de choses'; 'j'aurais pu écrire un chef-d'œuvre, les Guermantes m'en eussent moins fait d'honneur que de ce salut.'
appraisal_events.explanation: By declining to approach and offering only a discreet, correctly coded bow, the narrator wins extravagant, repeated admiration from the duc and duchesse, who relay it approvingly to his mother; the narrative frames this local mastery of aristocratic code as more prestigious to the Guermantes than any literary achievement.

status_effects.explanation: She is cast as a mere useful 'figurante' or 'fausse étoile' who fills out gatherings, implicitly beneath genuine grandes dames who need not attend everything to be recognized.
Her opinions of others are shown to shift with her invitation status rather than resting on stable independent judgment, undercutting her credibility as an evaluator.
The Guermantes couple's extravagant, widely repeated praise of his salute marks a clear local rise in his standing within their esteem.
His calculated restraint demonstrates fluent command of aristocratic social code ('le langage des cours'), itself part of what earns the acclaim.

ambiguities: The narrator explicitly calls the ambassadrice 'parfaitement sincère,' which complicates a reading of deliberate hypocrisy; her diminishment rests on being shown as a socially reactive, invitation-driven judge rather than a consciously insincere one, so the diminishment should be read as exposure of a mechanism rather than moral condemnation.
